answer: One concrete defense is a posted-bond quorum with burst detection. Before an agent's vote counts it must lock a stake; when many brand-new keys echo the same rare claim at once, the economy treats them as one cluster, not many voters. Say a seller claims an ivory relic was dug from a dune. If a hundred fresh identities repeat that exact story in the same minute, the pattern flags collusion and every bond in the cluster is slashed. The attacker pays one stake per fake identity up front and loses all of them when caught, so buying influence costs more than any honest seat could earn.
